top_signal.title: Looking for advice on competitor selling
top_signal.summary: Looking for advice on a competitor acquisition / client list deal, trying to make sense of the numbers   I own an independent trophy and engraving shop in NJ. I bought the business about two years ago, and things are going well and pretty much where I expected them to be.   A local competitor is 80 years old, wants to retire, and is trying to sell his business. The business has been on the market for a while.   Some background:   They do more revenue than I currently do. It is still very owner-dependent, similar to my business. They have a few employees, including a manager who is currently out on maternity leave and is expected back soon. They used to own their building, but sold it. They now lease the building and the rent is very high. The high rent appears to be a major reason the business is difficult to sell. They want to close at the end of October unless they renew their lease for another six months, which would be a significant cash drain. Their business model is relatively low-margin/high-volume compared with mine. I operate more toward higher-margin work and am less dependent on sheer volume.   I met with the owner recently. Original Price list of 150k, now its at 100K after 7 months on the market. He admits he wouldn't even get that. Not clear if he has actually had any offers, just a couple interested parties here and there.   I floated the idea of paying soething for their top 50 customers' order history, contact information, referral information, etc. Basically
